e-webhooks.1.evidence: Settings > Webhooks > Add Webhook (real fill + click): URL http://localhost:8911/walkstub/hook (the stack's request catcher), events Topic created + Reply created, Add Webhook -> notice 'Webhook saved.'; list row shows the URL, 'Topic created, Reply created', Active; Edit screen shows the 40-char signing secret with 'Use this to verify the X-Jetonomy-Signature header in your receiver.' wh-1.png

e-webhooks.2.evidence: Malformed 'not a url' -> browser validation 'Please enter a URL.' and no submit; https://no-such-host-zzq.invalid/hook -> 'Enter a valid webhook URL. The webhook was not saved.'; reachable stub URL with every event unticked -> 'Choose at least one event. A webhook with no events would never fire, so it was not saved.' wh-2.png

e-webhooks.3.evidence: POST /webhooks url ftp://x -> 400 jetonomy_webhook_url_invalid 'Invalid webhook URL.'; events ['bogus'] -> 400 jetonomy_webhook_events_invalid 'At least one valid event is required.'. Loopback (127.0.0.1) and private (10.0.0.5) URLs are already refused at create (400 Invalid webhook URL); to prove the delivery-time guard I inserted two such rows directly: /test returned success:false status_code:0 'A valid URL was not provided.' and a real post.created logged both in the deliveries table as status 0 'A valid URL was not provided.' with nothing reaching the catcher.

e-webhooks.4.evidence: POST /webhooks/81/test -> {success:true,status_code:200}; catcher got body {"event":"test","timestamp":...,"data":{"message":"This is a test webhook from Jetonomy."}} with X-Jetonomy-Signature sha256=... recomputed with the secret from the DB = match (SIG OK) and no X-Jetonomy-Event header; catcher set to 500 -> success:false,status_code:500; private/loopback host rows -> success:false,status_code:0,error 'A valid URL was not provided.'.

e-webhooks.5.evidence: bob (autologin) published 'Anyone using the new SMTP preset?' in General Discussion through the composer (the space has a required Operating system custom field, picked one); the catcher received post.created at the same second with data {id:15869,title,author_id:10,space_id:15,created_at}, header X-Jetonomy-Event: post.created and a signature that recomputes correctly (SIG OK). Note: delivery runs through Action Scheduler, so on this stack (no real cron) later jobs sat until a page request ran the queue (up to ~40s).

e-webhooks.6.evidence: With the webhook subscribed to all events, bob edited the topic (Edit > Save) -> one post.updated; replied -> one reply.created; More options > Delete > Confirm -> one post.deleted. Exactly one Action Scheduler job and one catcher request per action (1335/1337/1338 -> 3 log entries, no duplicates).

e-webhooks.7.evidence: Space 15 set to require_approval: bob's composer submit left the topic status=pending and the catcher stayed empty (no AS job); admin pressed Approve in Jetonomy > Moderation > Pending Topics -> exactly one post.created (id 15872, author_id 10). A topic marked Spam from the queue (id 15873) created no job, and a draft (composer 'Save as draft' then 'Save Draft', id 15874) created no job. Space setting restored.

e-webhooks.8.evidence: Private topic (is_private ticked, id 15871) -> no AS job and nothing at the catcher. Recorded: topics in private and hidden spaces DO fire. Admin REST topics in Customer Advisory Board (private, id 42) and Moderators' Room (hidden, id 43) each delivered post.created with the title and space_id to the external URL, so site owners should know any webhook leaks private-space titles. (bob is not a member of those spaces so used admin REST; the hook has no space-visibility filter.)

e-webhooks.9.evidence: General Discussion with allow_anonymous on: bob ticked 'Post anonymously' in the composer and posted 'Is anyone else struggling with caching on shared hosting?' (DB is_anonymous=1, author_id=10) -> catcher got post.created with author_id:0 and no author name. Space setting restored.

e-webhooks.10.evidence: Catcher answering 500, five real post.created events (admin REST topics) -> after the 5th delivery the webhook row had is_active 0, fail_count 5, last_status_code 500; the list shows Disabled, '3 seconds ago (500)' and failures 5 (wh-10.png). Re-enabled through Edit > Active > Update Webhook ('Webhook saved.', failures back to 0). Then fail_count set to 3, catcher back to 200, one new topic -> fail_count 0 and last_status_code 200.

e-webhooks.11.evidence: GET /webhooks/81/deliveries?per_page=2 -> 200, X-WP-Total 15, rows keys id,event,status_code,response,created_at. A real dispatch whose receiver returned 2000 bytes (pre_http_request stub inside wp eval, calling the real dispatch hook) stored a response of exactly 500 chars. Rows aged 31 days vs 29 days: running jetonomy_pro_prune_webhook_deliveries removed the 31-day row and kept the 29-day row (the daily job is registered via Queue::recurring).

e-webhooks.12.evidence: PATCH /webhooks/99999 -> 404 jetonomy_webhook_not_found 'Webhook not found.'. Created webhook 84, DELETE -> 200 {deleted:true}, PATCH of it -> 404, and later post.created / member events produced 0 delivery rows for id 84.
